title: Ordered projective-line projection square for the fixed scalar coefficient map
statement:
Fix a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ and a prime $\ell\ne p$. All schemes below are separated and finite type over $k$, and all maps are $k$-morphisms [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $A\to B$ be a unital map of finite commutative rings killed by powers of $\ell$, and choose $N=\ell^n\geq1$ annihilating both. On small ordinary etale sites use constant-ring module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] and $T_T=(-)_B=-\otimes^L_{A_T}B_T$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Write $D^b_{ctf}$ for bounded constructible complexes of finite Tor amplitude, as in [det-sp-et-proet-adjunction-transfer], and $R_T(1)=\mu_{N,T}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/N)_T}R_T$ for $R=A,B$ [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line]. For a standing base $S$, put $P=\mathbf P^1_S$, $q:P\to S$, $F_R=Rq_{*,R}$, $L_R=R_P(1)[2]$, $H_R=F_RL_R$ and $G_RK=q_R^*K\otimes_R^LL_R$. Give $q_R^*\dashv F_R$ its canonical geometric derived adjunction [def-kun-projection-formula-map]. Let $\beta_q:T_SF_A\to F_BT_P$ be the specified proper counit-transpose coefficient map [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility]. Write $m_{U,V}:T_S(U\otimes_A^LV)\xrightarrow{\sim}T_SU\otimes_B^LT_SV$ for the canonical scalar tensor comparison [def-pur-exceptional-coefficient-normalizations]. Let $\lambda:T_PL_A\xrightarrow{\sim}L_B$ be the balanced twist comparison, shifted by $[2]$, whose unshifted ordinary representative sends $(z\otimes a)\otimes b$ to $z\otimes\varphi(a)b$. Let $a_K:T_PG_AK\xrightarrow{\sim}G_BT_SK$ be the canonical scalar tensor comparison followed by the canonical inverse-image/scalar comparison on the first factor and $\lambda$ on the second [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Set $b=F_B(\lambda)\circ\beta_q(L_A)$. Define the ordered projection map by
$$\pi_{R,K}=F_R(\sigma)\circ\mathrm{PF}_q(L_R,K)\circ\sigma:K\otimes_R^LH_R\longrightarrow F_RG_RK,$$
where $\mathrm{PF}$ is the geometric counit-transpose map [def-kun-projection-formula-map] and $\sigma$ is derived tensor symmetry [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons]. Then, naturally for every $K\in D^b_{ctf}(S_{et},A)$, the following equality holds in $D(S_{et},B)$:
$$F_B(a_K)\circ\beta_q(G_AK)\circ T_S(\pi_{A,K})=\pi_{B,T_SK}\circ(1_{T_SK}\otimes b)\circ m_{K,H_A}.$$
No flatness or finite projective dimension of $B$ over $A$ is assumed.

proof.text: View coefficient change as a square of ringed topoi. Its upper corners are $(P_{et},A_P)$ and $(P_{et},B_P)$, its lower corners $(S_{et},A_S)$ and $(S_{et},B_S)$. The vertical morphisms are $q_A,q_B$ and the horizontal morphisms are the identity geometric morphisms with structural maps $A_T\to B_T$. These are ringed morphisms by [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]; the square commutes since inverse image carries the constant coefficient homomorphism on $S$ to that on $P$. The horizontal derived pullbacks are exactly $T_P,T_S$ by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Denote the canonical comparison by $c_K:q_B^*T_SK\xrightarrow{\sim}T_Pq_A^*K$. The composition and 2-isomorphism clauses of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] give this comparison with the canonical tensor normalizations. The exchange of this square has adjunct $T_P(\varepsilon_{A,E})\circ c_{F_AE}$ by [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. This is also the defining adjunct of the specified proper coefficient map in [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility]. The adjunction Hom bijection therefore identifies the exchange with the actual $\beta_q(E)$, rather than just an isomorphism with the same source and target.

proof.text:
Write $p_R(E,K)=\mathrm{PF}_q(E,K)$, and let $m^P$ denote the scalar tensor comparison on $P$. Put $d_{E,K}=(1\otimes c_K^{-1})\circ m^P_{E,q_A^*K}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence] to the ringed square of step 1. The vertical projection maps there are exactly $p_R$ because their adjunct is counit tensor identity, the definition in [def-kun-projection-formula-map]. Its equality reads
$$F_B(d_{E,K})\circ\beta_q(E\otimes q_A^*K)\circ T_S(p_A(E,K))=p_B(T_PE,T_SK)\circ(\beta_q(E)\otimes1)\circ m_{F_AE,K}.$$
The general lemma imposes no cartesianness assumption, so it applies to this coefficient square. Its tensors and comparisons are the canonical ones. In particular the scalar tensor comparison is the specified balanced comparison of [def-pur-exceptional-coefficient-normalizations], since scalar extension is the horizontal derived pullback. No inversion of $\beta_q$ or of a projection morphism occurs.

source.place: Tag 0E48, remark-compatible-with-diagram; Tag 0B56, equation-projection-formula-map. Agent-written specialization to coefficient change and ordered symmetry.

proof.text:
For $E,K$ with $R$-coefficients define $o_R(E,K)=F_R(\sigma_{E,q_R^*K})\circ p_R(E,K)\circ\sigma_{K,F_RE}$. Put $e_{K,E}=(c_K^{-1}\otimes1)\circ m^P_{q_A^*K,E}$. Scalar pullback is symmetric monoidal by [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons], so
$$m_{F_AE,K}\,T_S(\sigma_{K,F_AE})=\sigma_{T_SK,T_SF_AE}\,m_{K,F_AE},$$
$$e_{K,E}\,T_P(\sigma_{E,q_A^*K})=\sigma_{T_PE,q_B^*T_SK}\,d_{E,K}.$$
Precompose step 2 by $T_S(\sigma_{K,F_AE})$ and postcompose by $F_B(\sigma_{T_PE,q_B^*T_SK})$. Naturality of $\beta_q$ moves $T_SF_A(\sigma)$ to $F_BT_P(\sigma)$; naturality of symmetry moves $\beta_q(E)\otimes1$ to $1\otimes\beta_q(E)$. Substituting the two displayed identities yields
$$F_B(e_{K,E})\circ\beta_q(q_A^*K\otimes E)\circ T_S(o_A(E,K))=o_B(T_PE,T_SK)\circ(1\otimes\beta_q(E))\circ m_{K,F_AE}.$$
This is substitution of naturality and the two symmetric-monoidal identities, with no new geometric claim.

source.place: Tag 0E48, remark-compatible-with-diagram; Tag 0B56, equation-projection-formula-map. Agent-written specialization to coefficient change and ordered symmetry.

proof.text:
Take $E=L_A$. Then $o_A(L_A,K)=\pi_{A,K}$. Postcompose step 3 with $F_B(1_{q_B^*T_SK}\otimes\lambda)$. The ordered projection morphism is natural in $E$: for $u:E\to E'$,
$$F_B(1\otimes u)\circ o_B(E,T_SK)=o_B(E',T_SK)\circ(1\otimes F_B(u)).$$
Indeed, expanding $o_B$ by [def-kun-projection-formula-map], this is counit naturality for $u$, naturality of the tensor comparison, and naturality of the two symmetries [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons]. Apply this identity to $u=\lambda:T_PL_A\to L_B$. On the left, $(1\otimes\lambda)\circ e_{K,L_A}$ is exactly $a_K$ by its defining ordered tensor/pullback construction. On the right, $F_B(\lambda)\circ\beta_q(L_A)=b$ and $o_B(L_B,T_SK)=\pi_{B,T_SK}$. Functoriality of $F_B$ and of tensor therefore gives
$$F_B(a_K)\circ\beta_q(G_AK)\circ T_S(\pi_{A,K})=\pi_{B,T_SK}\circ(1\otimes b)\circ m_{K,H_A}.$$
The argument uses the specified $\lambda$, including its shift; it never replaces it by an arbitrary trivialization of the twist.

source.place: Tag 0E48, remark-compatible-with-diagram; Tag 0B56, equation-projection-formula-map. Agent-written specialization to coefficient change and ordered symmetry.

proof.text: All maps used above are natural in $K$: the geometric adjunction and its projection map are natural by their explicit unit/counit formula [def-kun-projection-formula-map], the coefficient map is natural by [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility], and the scalar/pullback and symmetry comparisons are natural by [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons]. Thus the equality restricts naturally to the stated $D^b_{ctf}$ inputs. The calculation took place in the ambient ordinary unbounded derived categories; the ringed exchange coherence has no cartesianness condition and scalar extension is everywhere defined without flatness by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Accordingly no finite projective dimension of $B$ or bounded free resolution of $B$ was used.
